channel.title: 100 Doors to Recursion
channel.description: One door a day for 100 days into the things I've made with AI, from my first app to the system I run now.

item.title: Day 20: Precompact Protector: keep your place through a compaction
item.description: precompact-protector: two Claude Code hooks that save the last 40 turns before compaction and hand back your last request and the files in play after. Something to try: Merge settings-snippet.json into ~/.claude/settings.json with the real path; nothing to install.

item.title: Day 19: Field Audit: grade your AI setup with receipts
item.description: Field Audit: one paste-in prompt that has Claude Code audit the AI system on your machine, scoring 12 parts with a receipt each and naming every gap. Something to try: Paste the prompt file into Claude Code at your system root; post your scorecard as an issue to join the ledger.

item.title: Day 18: The Spine Pattern: memory that never erases
item.description: The Spine Pattern: 13 principles, a 6-part checklist and a standard-library engine for an append-only log with provenance, typed edges and supersede. Something to try: Run the README's ledger story on a fresh clone: three values kept, two SUPERSEDES edges, nothing erased.

item.title: Day 17: Blind Council: five models argue, one settles
item.description: Blind Council: five models answer on their own, cross-examine each other as MEMBER-A to E, and a sixth model that never debated settles it. Something to try: bun install, put an OpenRouter key in .env, then bun run council "your question" (about one to two dollars for a six-seat run).

item.title: Day 16: CorpusSync: search what you already know
item.description: CorpusSync: ingest notes, documents and YouTube captions into a local Qdrant store, search by meaning and by exact word behind a relevance gate, and get answers from a local Ollama model with numbered sources. Something to try: pip install -e . in a venv, ollama pull nomic-embed-text, then corpussync ingest ./notes --corpus notes and corpussync search.

item.title: Day 15: Changelog Digest: your changelog becomes content
item.description: changelog-digest again (the Door 8 tool): a Python script that reads a markdown changelog and writes a hook, a short story and video ideas. Something to try: Run python3 changelog_digest.py examples/sample-changelog.md --date 2026-03-14 --dry-run to see the prompt without an API key.

item.title: Day 14: ShipGate: no leaked keys go public
item.description: ShipGate: one shell script, ship-gate.sh, that runs gitleaks and trufflehog over the full history and checks the LICENSE, a raw .env and attribution, with one exit code. Something to try: brew install gitleaks trufflehog, put ship-gate.sh on your PATH and run it in a repo before it goes public.

item.title: Day 13: Review gate: fresh eyes on every push
item.description: review-gate: one Python file (standard library only), an install script that writes a pre-push hook, and 24 tests. Something to try: Run install.sh inside your project to add the pre-push hook; it needs the Claude Code CLI signed in and Python 3.10 or newer.

item.title: Day 12: Hooks over reminders: checks on every agent edit
item.description: harness-guard: four quality hooks plus the safety hooks for Claude Code, each a short shell script you can read first. Something to try: Clone it and run ./install.sh, or merge just the four quality-hook lines from settings.example.json into ~/.claude/settings.json.

item.title: Day 11: TabMap: why 200 tabs are open
item.description: TabMap: captures your open tabs, labels each by intent, project, stale or solved, then offers a cleanup that lists before it closes anything. Something to try: Clone it, pip install -r requirements.txt, run python3 -m tab_intel.capture, then preview the cleanup with auto_cleaner.py --dry-run.

item.title: Day 10: Ecosystem MCP: research npm packages from inside Claude Code
item.description: The repo: research, compare and security-check npm packages from inside Claude Code. Something to try: Add it to Claude Code and ask it to compare two packages before you install either.

item.title: Day 9: block-destructive: a Claude Code hook that stops destructive shell commands before the agent runs them
item.description: The hook: refuses rm -rf on root or home, force-pushes to main, git push --no-verify and curl piped into sh; a seatbelt for accidents, not a sandbox. Something to try: Copy block-destructive.sh to ~/.claude/hooks and add it as a PreToolUse hook on Bash.

item.title: Day 8: The changelog that becomes content
item.description: changelog-digest: turn a day of changelog entries into a hook, a short story and video ideas. Something to try: Run the dry run on the sample changelog, then on your own.

item.title: Day 7: The perfection pass: ask for two critique passes before you look
item.description: pp2p and pp3p, two Claude Code skills: two or three critique passes, then a polish. Something to try: Before you read your agent's next piece of work, ask it for two critique passes that try to break it, then a polish.

item.title: Day 6: My Claude Code config, and the ramp: a 53-second first session in May, then 146 sessions from November 8 to December 11
item.description: claude-config-public: the operating-rules template. Something to try: Copy it to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and fill in the 5 placeholders.

item.title: Day 5: treehouse: a git worktree pool for running several coding agents side by side
item.description: treehouse, one bash file that needs only git: spin a worktree per agent, glance at which are dirty on one screen, and sweep only the clean, merged ones. Something to try: Run treehouse spin 3, then treehouse glance.

item.title: Day 4: FriendForm: a form friends fill out from a link
item.description: A blank intake form to copy into any form tool. Something to try: Take one questionnaire you send around as a document, rebuild it from these sections and cut every question you would not act on.

item.title: Day 3: My CRM, started on Replit from two pasted documents
item.description: dataguard: checks a SQL database for orphaned records and dates out of order (link goes up when it is ready). Something to try: Pick one table in a database you own and count the rows that point at a record that no longer exists.

item.title: Day 2: WebPerformanceToolkit: my first app in git, and its 33 hours of simulated scores
item.description: The first prompt template: twelve sections plus the real-data line. Something to try: Before your next build, fill in at least sections 1, 4, 5 and 6, then paste the whole thing as your first message.

item.title: Day 1: RobotTales: bedtime stories where robot siblings teach if/else, loops and variables
item.description: A bedtime-story prompt that teaches one coding idea. Something to try: Paste it into any chat model, fill in the three brackets, and read what comes back before you read it aloud.
